abstract:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether a wearable-enabled prehabilitation and rehabilitation pathway can improve recovery and post-operative outcomes in adults undergoing surgery for pancreatic cancer or related pancreatic/periampullary conditions.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can a digitally-enhanced prehabilitation and rehabilitation pathway (Prehab4Cancer exercise, nutrition and wellbeing support combined with wearable remote monitoring) reduce morbidity in patients undergoing pancreatic cancer surgery, compared with current standard of care (SoC), which does not include a structured prehabilitation or rehabilitation pathway for these patients?

Researchers will compare patients receiving the wearable-enabled pathway with a matched historical control group who received standard care to determine whether the intervention is associated with improved surgical and recovery outcomes.

Participants will:

Provide informed consent and complete baseline assessments and questionnaires. Take part in the Greater Manchester Prehab4Cancer programme before surgery, including personalised exercise, nutritional support, and wellbeing support.

Wear a Corsano CardioWatch device to continuously monitor physiological and activity data.

Use home monitoring equipment, including weight scales and blood pressure monitoring devices.

Complete questionnaires and participant logs during prehabilitation and recovery.

Receive regular support from the research team during participation. Undergo pancreatic surgery and receive standard NHS perioperative care. Continue wearable monitoring and rehabilitation after hospital discharge. Be followed for up to 12 months after surgery using routine clinical data to assess recovery, complications, hospital utilisation, and survival.

Optionally participate in a focus group to discuss their experiences of wearable-enabled care.

POWR-PaC is single-centre, non-randomised study with a prospective intervention cohort and a retrospective, propensity-matched control cohort receiving standard care, evaluating effectiveness of a digitally-enhanced prehabilitation and rehabilitation pathway in patients undergoing surgical resection of pancreatic cancer or related pancreatic/periampullary conditions at Manchester Royal Infirmary, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust. The study will test whether adding wearable devices and remote monitoring to an existing prehabilitation and rehabilitation pathway is acceptable, feasible, and associated with better recovery after surgery.

The main research question is whether a digitally enhanced prehabilitation programme can reduce post-operative complications in patients undergoing pancreatic cancer surgery, compared with standard care. The null hypothesis is that there will be no difference in post-operative morbidity between patients receiving digitally enhanced prehabilitation/rehabilitation and those receiving standard care. The alternative hypothesis is that digitally enhanced prehabilitation/rehabilitation will reduce post-operative morbidity, measured by the number of complications within 30 and 90 days after surgery. Secondary questions will explore mortality, days alive and out of hospital, length of recovery, wearable data completeness and usefulness, and patient and staff experience of the devices.

This design has been chosen because prehabilitation is already used in cancer pathways and the study intervention builds on an existing Greater Manchester Prehab4Cancer service rather than replacing standard NHS care. Wearable devices may provide additional information about activity, sleep, vital signs, weight and recovery, but more evidence is needed about whether this is useful and acceptable in this patient group. A prospective design allows patients' experiences, device use and recovery to be followed in real time. A comparison group is included because surgical outcomes can vary between patients, and the study needs to compare outcomes against patients who received standard care without the digitally enhanced pathway. There is no placebo group. All participants will continue to receive normal clinical care, and no surgical or cancer treatment decisions will be changed because of study participation.

Up to 60 patients will be recruited to the intervention arm. Patients will be identified after the multidisciplinary team has agreed that surgery is appropriate and the clinical team considers that they may be suitable for the study. Patients will be given a Participant Information Sheet and will have at least 24 hours to consider participation. They will be able to ask questions before deciding whether to take part. If they wish to proceed, written informed consent will be taken by an appropriately delegated member of the research team, usually during a face-to-face clinical or research appointment at Manchester Royal Infirmary.

After consent, participants will have a baseline study visit. At this visit, eligibility will be confirmed, a study ID will be allocated, baseline clinical information will be recorded, and participants will complete questionnaires about quality of life, physical function, activity, symptoms, self-efficacy and digital readiness. Functional assessments will also be carried out, including a 6-minute walk test, sit-to-stand test, hand grip strength assessment, nutritional assessment and frailty assessment. These assessments are intended to give a picture of the participant's health and physical function before surgery.

Participants will then be given study devices and shown how to use them. These will include a Corsano CardioWatch wearable wrist device, body weight scales, and a blood pressure monitor used to support blood pressure calibration where needed. Participants will be given written and verbal instructions, including how to charge the device and when to remove it, for example for certain scans. The wearable device will collect information such as activity, heart rate, respiration rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, sleep and other physiological measurements.

During the prehabilitation phase, participants will take part in the Greater Manchester Prehab4Cancer programme before their operation. This is a personalised programme involving exercise, nutritional support and wellbeing support. Participants will usually attend supervised sessions at their local leisure centre, with support from trained exercise specialists. They will be encouraged to attend regular sessions before surgery, with activities tailored to their ability and clinical condition. During this period, they will continue to wear the study device and use the home monitoring equipment.

While participants are in the prehabilitation phase, a member of the research team will contact them approximately once per week by telephone. These calls are intended to support participants, answer questions about the devices, encourage engagement with the study, and identify any issues. Participants may also complete short questionnaires or self-logs about symptoms, wellbeing, device use and their experience of the programme. These may be completed electronically or on paper, depending on participant preference and accessibility needs.

When the participant is admitted to hospital for surgery, the research team will carry out a brief repeat assessment before the operation where feasible. Participants will continue to receive their normal NHS surgical and perioperative care throughout admission. The study does not alter the operation, anaesthetic care, oncology care or clinical decision-making.

After discharge from hospital, participants will move into the rehabilitation phase. They will continue to use the wearable device and home monitoring equipment while completing their post-operative recovery programme. They will complete further questionnaires at the end of rehabilitation and during follow-up. Routine clinical information about their recovery, complications, readmissions, mortality and days alive and out of hospital will be collected from the electronic health record. Follow-up will continue for up to 12 months after surgery.

At the end of their participation in the device-supported pathway, participants will return the devices either in person or by courier. Devices will be cleaned and reset. Participants will not be able to keep the study devices.

The study will also include a comparison group of up to 60 patients who previously underwent similar surgery at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust from 2022 onwards and received standard care. These patients will not be contacted and will not undergo any additional procedures. Their routinely collected electronic health record data will be used to create a matched comparison group. Matching will use factors such as age, sex, diagnosis, operation type, comorbidities, frailty or functional status where available, nutritional status, neoadjuvant treatment and time from MDT decision to surgery. This approach is intended to make the intervention and comparison groups as similar as possible, so that any differences in outcomes can be interpreted more fairly. All potential control patients will be checked against the NHS National Data Opt-Out before their data are used.

A small number of participants may also be invited to take part in an optional focus group after they have used the wearable device for at least 14 days. Healthcare professionals and Prehab4Cancer exercise specialists involved in the pathway may also be invited to separate focus groups. The focus groups will explore people's views on the wearable devices, remote monitoring, barriers and benefits, and how this type of technology could be improved for future care. Focus groups will be optional, will require separate written consent, and will usually last approximately 60 to 90 minutes. They will take place in a private meeting room at Manchester Royal Infirmary. Focus groups will be audio-recorded with consent, transcribed, anonymised and analysed thematically.

The planned sample size is up to 120 patients in total: up to 60 participants in the prospective intervention arm and up to 60 matched standard-care controls. This sample size is based on the expected number of eligible patients seen in the pancreatic cancer surgical pathway and the feasibility of recruitment over approximately 18 months. It is expected that around five eligible patients are seen each month, and that recruiting 60 participants is achievable within the recruitment period.

The broad timetable is as follows. The study will recruit participants for up to 18 months. Each intervention participant will be involved from enrolment before surgery, through prehabilitation, surgery, discharge and rehabilitation, with clinical outcome follow-up continuing for up to 12 months after surgery. After recruitment and live participant follow-up are complete, the research team will clean and analyse the data, interpret the findings, prepare a final study report, and share the results through participant summaries, academic publication and/or conference presentation. The overall study duration is approximately 30 months.

The quantitative analysis will compare outcomes between the digitally enhanced pathway and the matched standard-care group. The main outcome will be the number of post-operative complications within 30 and 90 days. Secondary outcomes will include mortality, days alive and out of hospital, wearable data completeness, patient adherence, and questionnaire outcomes. Wearable-derived data will also be explored to understand whether patterns in activity, physiology or recovery may help predict outcomes.

Qualitative data from focus groups, feedback forms and participant logs will be analysed using thematic analysis. This means the research team will read the transcripts carefully, identify repeated ideas or patterns, develop themes, and use these themes to understand participants' and staff members' experiences of the devices and digitally supported care pathway.

There are no planned interim analyses that will change participant care or the conduct of the study. Recruitment, adverse events, participant burden and study progress will be reviewed regularly by the research team and Trial Management Group. Any safety concerns or required changes will be managed in line with sponsor, REC and HRA requirements.

Several steps will be taken to reduce bias. The comparison group will be selected using propensity score matching to reduce differences between groups at baseline. Standardised questionnaires and predefined clinical outcomes will be used where possible. Clinical outcome data will be obtained from the electronic health record rather than relying only on participant recall. For qualitative work, a semi-structured topic guide will be used to ensure that similar topics are covered across focus groups, while still allowing participants to raise issues important to them. Transcripts will be anonymised, and themes will be discussed within the research team to reduce the risk that findings reflect only one researcher's interpretation.

Patient and public involvement has informed the development of the study. Previous patient and public contributor input from related wearable monitoring and prehabilitation work at the Trust influenced the choice to use non-invasive wearable devices, avoid extra hospital-based tests where possible, integrate research activity with routine care, include patient-reported outcomes, allow flexible visit windows and include focus groups to understand patient experience. This has helped ensure that the study is designed around what patients are likely to find understandable and acceptable during a difficult surgical cancer pathway.
key_points_ko: 췌장암 및 췌주위 질환으로 수술이 확정된 환자 60명을 대상으로 디지털 사전·사후 재활 프로그램을 적용합니다.
Corsano CardioWatch 착용형 기기와 원격 모니터링 장비를 통해 수술 전후 활동량 및 생체 신호를 연속 측정합니다.
수술 후 30일 및 90일 이내의 합병증 발생률 감소 여부를 과거 표준 치료 대조군과 비교 평가합니다.
summary_ko: 췌장암 및 췌주위 암 수술 예정 환자를 대상으로 웨어러블 기기를 활용한 디지털 사전·사후 재활 프로그램의 효과를 평가하는 연구입니다. 연구 참여자는 수술 전후로 운동, 영양, 심리 지원 프로그램에 참여하고 착용형 생체 모니터링 기기를 사용하게 됩니다. 연구진은 이 프로그램을 이수한 환자군과 과거 표준 치료를 받은 환자군을 비교하여 수술 후 합병증 감소 및 회복 향상 효과를 확인하고자 합니다.
title: Wearable-Supported Prehabilitation and Rehabilitation for Patients Undergoing Surgery for Pancreatic Cancer
title_ko: 췌장암 수술 환자를 위한 웨어러블 기기 기반 수술 전후 재활 치료 임상시험

trial.eligibility_ko:
선정 기준:
• 만 18세 이상 성인
• 자발적으로 연구 참여 동의서를 작성할 수 있는 환자
• 본인 또는 보호자의 도움으로 연구 기기를 사용할 수 있는 환자
• 췌장암, 원위부 담도암, 팽대부암, 십이지장암, 췌장 전암성 병변(IPMN 등)으로 수술이 확정된 환자
• 재활 프로그램에 참여할 수 있을 만큼 임상적으로 안정적인 환자
• 스마트폰 또는 태블릿 기기를 소유하고 있는 환자

제외 기준:
• 자발적 동의 제공 능력이 없거나 동의하지 않는 환자
• 불합병성 심혈관 질환(불안정 협심증, 최근 심근경색, 최근 뇌졸중, 신규 심장 부정맥)이 있는 환자
• 원격 모니터링을 위한 통신 환경(모바일 데이터 또는 Wi-Fi)이 없는 환자
• 72시간 이내 입원이 필요할 정도로 임상 상태가 불안정한 환자
• 연구 절차 준수를 방해할 수 있는 신체적, 정신적, 사회적 문제가 있는 환자
trial.eligibility_text:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult patients aged 18 years or older.
* Able to provide informed consent.
* Able to use the study devices independently or with support from a carer.
* Approved for pancreatic cancer surgery, including patients undergoing surgery for:

Pancreatic cancer Distal cholangiocarcinoma Ampullary carcinoma Duodenal carcinoma Premalignant pancreatic lesions, including Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasms (IPMNs).

* Clinically stable and considered suitable to participate in the prehabilitation and rehabilitation programme.
* Owns a smartphone or tablet device

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unable or unwilling to provide informed consent.
* Lacks capacity to provide informed consent.
* Unstable angina pectoris.
* Recent myocardial infarction.
* Recent cerebrovascular accident (stroke).
* New cardiac arrhythmia.
* Social, physical, mental health, or substance misuse issues that, in the opinion of the investigator, would jeopardise adherence to study procedures or study contact.
* No infrastructure for remote monitoring (no access to either mobile signal or Wi-Fi).
* Clinically unstable or likely to require hospital admission within the next 72 hours.
* Unable to use the study devices and no carer or support person is available to assist.
